work, piece (of art, literature, or the like)

Werkzeug.et: From Middle High German wercziuc, werchziuc, (also as Middle High German wercgeziuc, werchgeziuc > German Werkgezeug); equivalent to Werk (“work”) + Zeug (“gear, equipment”).

Wermelskirchen.et: From Middle Low German Werenboldeskirken (around the year 1150).

Werwolf.et: From Middle High German wërwolf, from Old High German wërwolf, from Proto-West Germanic *werawulf (literally “man-wolf”).

s: a common surname originating as a patronymic

wer den Schaden hat, braucht für den Spo.et: Literally, “he who has loss (or harm), need not arrange for mockery”, meaning that he will get it automatically.

Werber.et: From Middle High German wërbære, equivalent to werben + -er.

Humorous alteration of a passage in Goethe's “Wilhelm Meister”: Wer nie sein Brot mit Tränen aß, / wer nie die kummervollen Nächte / auf seinem Bette weinend saß, / der kennt euch …

s: verst (old Russian unit of length, roughly equivalent to a kilometre)

s: hards, tow, oakum (short, fallen-off fibres of flax or hemp)

Wergeld.et: From Middle High German wergelt, from Old High German werigelt, from Proto-West Germanic *werageld (literally “man-money”).

promotional item, promotional article, promotional product

A stable securities market is essential for the economic power of a modern industrial society, as it directs the flow of capital.

Companies in the knowledge sector use the securities market to increase their solvency for future investments through the issuance of shares.
securities trading (the professional buying and selling of financial instruments such as stocks, bonds, and derivatives)
Der organisierte Wertpapierhandel bildet das Rückgrat der Kapitalallokation innerhalb einer modernen Industriegesellschaft und sichert deren Wirtschaftskraft.
Organized securities trading forms the backbone of capital allocation within a modern industrial society and secures its economic power.
Durch den elektronischen Wertpapierhandel können Investoren im Wissenssektor ihre Zahlungskraft nahezu in Echtzeit umschichten, um auf Marktveränderungen zu reagieren.
Through electronic securities trading, investors in the knowledge sector can shift their solvency almost in real-time to react to market changes.
recoverability, intrinsic value, value retention (the quality of an asset to retain its value or to be convertible into a predictable amount of cash)

After commodity market prices stabilized, the company had to perform a significant write-up on its inventories.
Das geltende Anschaffungswertprinzip begrenzt die Wertaufholung auf maximal die ursprünglichen Anschaffungs- oder Herstellungskosten.
The applicable historical cost principle limits the recovery in value to a maximum of the original acquisition or production costs.
impairment, depreciation, diminution in value (a reduction in the book value of an asset because its fair value has fallen below its carrying amount)
Aufgrund des technologischen Fortschritts musste eine außerplanmäßige Wertminderung auf die alten Produktionsmaschinen vorgenommen werden.
Due to technological progress, an unscheduled impairment had to be made on the old production machines.
Die Wertminderung des Firmenwerts (Goodwill) wird jährlich durch einen Impairment-Test überprüft.
The diminution in value of goodwill is reviewed annually through an impairment test.
securities fund (an investment fund that invests its assets in various types of securities such as stocks or bonds)

A broadly diversified securities fund reduces risk by spreading across different asset classes and issuers.
Gesetzliche Vorgaben regeln genau, welche Arten von Aktiva ein Wertpapierfonds zur Sicherstellung der Liquidität halten darf.
Legal requirements strictly regulate which types of assets a securities fund may hold to ensure liquidity.
securities holdings, securities assets (the portion of total assets held in the form of stocks, bonds, or other tradable financial instruments)
